## Two Changes to Selective Availability

Selective Availability deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security. The U.S. government stopped using the feature in May 2000, at President Bill Clinton’s direction, to make civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide.

A separate change was announced in September 2007: the future GPS III generation would be procured without Selective Availability. This was not the operational switch that took place in 2000. It specified the feature’s omission from a future generation, making the 2000 policy durable for GPS III.
